narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an overwhelming probability, it was high enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

Your application was denied primarily because of three key factors that carried the most weight in the decision. First, your credit history of critical or other existing credits pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk. Although this history is fairly common (33% of approved applicants share it), the model viewed it as a warning sign compared with the majority who have smoothly paid existing loans.

Second, the short 11-month duration you requested actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. Most approved applicants request almost twice as long (19 months on average), so your modest timeframe was seen positively.

Third, the status of your checking account (currently between 0 and 200 DM) was the factor that most increased your risk score. Only 18% of approved applicants sit in this bracket, while nearly 60% have no checking account at all. The model interpreted this modest balance as a sign of limited financial buffer.

In short, your credit history and current checking-account level outweighed the positive signal from your short loan request. 

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a cleaner credit history, maintaining a stronger checking-account balance, and perhaps waiting until your financial picture looks more stable before reapplying. (218 words)
